summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes and a history of chronic nausea and vomiting was admitted for several days of early morning vomiting, including a small amount of blood. She was unable to tolerate oral intake initially and was managed with IV fluids and anti-nausea medications. Imaging showed no acute abnormalities. An EGD revealed mild esophageal varices and stable gastric findings, with no active bleeding. Her aspirin was held due to hematemesis, and she was started on Lisinopril for newly recognized hypertension. Her diet was advanced as nausea resolved, and she tolerated full liquids by discharge. She was discharged home with plans to follow up for variceal evaluation, lab monitoring on Lisinopril, and discussion about restarting aspirin.
problems: Diabetes with renal manifestations, type I [juvenile type], uncontrolled
Esophageal varices without mention of bleeding
Nephritis and nephropathy, not specified as acute or chronic, in diseases classified elsewhere
